title.narrative: Rapid humanitarian response to the flooding emergency

description.narrative: On 9 November 2024 heavy rains in the Colombian department of Choco caused a serious emergency situation with 27 of the 31 municipalities affected by flooding. Initial reports were that more than 150,000 people of 37,577 families lost homes, household goods, crops, productive units and livestock. Although the department of Chocó in Colombia is one of the places with the highest rainfall in the world, usually with heavy rains in the months of October and November, on this occasion the La Niña phenomenon, together with the impacts of the climate crisis have caused rivers and streams to overflow, which has caused damage to infrastructure and housing, as well as damaging economic activities such as agriculture and fishing. Chocó, located on Colombia's Pacific coast, considering that it is one of the most vulnerable departments in Colombia due to its extreme economic poverty, poor infrastructure and limited presence of the Colombian state. Despite its rich biodiversity and natural resources, it faces a series of socio-economic challenges that have limited its development. The department is mainly inhabited by Afro, indigenous and mestizo populations that have been victims of serious human rights violations during decades of armed conflict. This project seeks to support 450 families (around 2250 people) with food kits, as well as providing first aid kits and training on how to use them, supplementing limited aid provided by the Colombian State by filling essential gaps in health and food.
